---
name: paigasus-main-strict-checks-dependabot
description: "paigasus-core main ruleset: required 'moon ci' check with strict up-to-date-branch policy; how that interacts with dependabot merge trains"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 6c9d3b43-69b7-4125-88cf-e1da3886418a
  modified: 2026-10-19T08:54:53.064Z

paigasus-core's `main` ruleset requires the `moon ci` status check with
`strict_required_status_checks_policy: true` (branch must contain latest main), plus
deletion/non-fast-forward protection. There is no required-review rule — `gh pr merge
--squash` works directly once checks are green and the branch is current.

**Why:** merging PRs in sequence invalidates the next PR's merge eligibility
(`mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`, "base branch policy prohibits the merge") until its branch
contains the new main head.

**How to apply:** for dependabot merge trains, merge one PR, then wait — dependabot
auto-rebases its remaining PRs onto new main (check `headRefOid` changed) and `moon ci`
re-runs; merge when green. BUT dependabot stops rebasing a branch once anyone else pushes
to it — then use `PUT /repos/.../pulls/N/update-branch` (GitHub-signed merge of main into
the branch) and wait for the re-run. Its `expected_head_sha` must be the FULL 40-character SHA:
a short SHA returns HTTP 422 "expected head sha didn't match current head ref" (PR 329,
2026-09-27). The same call also works for your own feature PR right after `gh pr create`, and it
avoids a local rebase that would re-sign every commit. Watch main after each merge: push-to-main triggers
`CI`, `prebuild`, and sometimes `Dependency Graph`.

**`gh pr update-branch --rebase` is the right tool** (avoids a merge commit, so the commitlint
parity gate only ever sees dependabot's own commit) — **but it makes dependabot REGENERATE the
PR**, re-resolving deps to newest-available and blowing past the npm cooldown. See
[[pnpm-minimum-release-age]] for the resulting catch-22 and its fix.

A full 7-PR train (2026-08-05) took ~6 serial CI cycles at ~10-20 min each. The local
`.lefthook/pre-push/check-branch.sh` enforces `^feature/[a-z0-9._-]+$` (no Linear key
required; `main` and `dependabot/*` are exempt) and validates the CURRENT branch name — so to
push a fix onto a dependabot branch, rename the local branch to match it first.

**update-branch can leave `rs/Cargo.lock` stale** (PR 412, 2026-10-19): main moved `syn` to
3.0.9, the GitHub merge kept the PR's `pyo3-macros` entries on `syn 3.0.6`, and `--locked`
then failed the lockfile-integrity step and `build + smoke`. Fix: run `cargo metadata` in `rs/`
on the merged branch and commit the lock. Check this after every update-branch on a cargo PR.

Related: [[paigasus-commit-signing-1password]] (API-commit fallback when 1Password is locked),
[[dependabot-cargo-lockfile-truncation]] (never merge a cargo PR without checking its lock).

`repo:deny` fails on `main` since the CI run of 2026-11-17 20:11 UTC (run 44166688260). It also fails Dependabot PR 487.

+++ Agent notes

The advisory is not a vulnerability. It recommends `jiff` or `time`. The PR 487 diff (redis 1.8.2, libc 0.2.191) does not touch chrono.

# iam-tool-policy-sets, section 5.1). It has its own Cargo.lock. It cannot inherit
# `[workspace.package]` from `rs/`, so it restates the edition, the rust-version and the lints.

## Dependabot PRs

- **PR 487 was red because of a new advisory, not because of its bump.** RUSTSEC-2026-0543 says that `chrono` is unmaintained. It also made `main` red. PR 489 (SMA-784) adds a waiver for it in `rs/deny.toml`, and `main` is green again.

- npm patches: eslint, typescript-eslint 8.73, playwright 1.65.1, msw 3.0.6 and others.
- Python: openai 3.55.1, anthropic 2.10.0 and httpx2. Our pins are exact, so Dependabot does not move them.

- Node 26: this is the change that unblocks `semantic-release` 26 and `@types/node` 26.
- pnpm 12, helm 4, release-plz 0.4.

- jsonwebtoken 11.1.0 → 12.0.0 (the `rust_crypto` backend stays)
- async-nats 0.52 → 0.53.0

testcontainers stays at 0.27. testcontainers-modules 0.15.0 is the newest release, and it requires testcontainers ^0.27. The move to 0.28 waits for a modules release.

### reqwest 0.13

- reqwest 0.13 removed `rustls-tls` and `rustls-tls-native-roots`. Its `rustls` feature pulls aws-lc-rs as a second crypto provider, so the workspace uses `rustls-no-provider`.
- reqwest panics at `Client::build()` if no provider is installed. Each client build installs the ring provider first. The two production builders do this in `base_builder`.
- **Trust change.** reqwest 0.13 verifies with `rustls-platform-verifier`, which uses the OS trust store. The compiled-in webpki-roots floor is gone. `add_root_certificate` still adds roots to the OS store; it does not replace it. On Linux, an empty store with no extra bundle is now a client build error, so it fails closed. The runtime image includes the chisel `ca-certificates_data` slice (`/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, 120 certificates).
- The `form` feature is now explicit (only `keycloak_e2e` uses it).
- `rs/deny.toml` allows `webpki-root-certs` (CDLA-Permissive-2.0, the same data licence as `webpki-roots`). It comes from `rustls-platform-verifier`.

### jsonwebtoken 12

No source change. A diff of 11.1.0 and 12.0.0 shows that each change makes validation stricter: claim type checks, `crit` header rejection, and rsa 0.10 key-size limits of 1024 to 8192 bits. The `Validation` defaults do not change.

### async-nats 0.53

`add_root_certificates` now implies `require_tls(true)`. New config checks reject a CA bundle with a non-`tls://` URL, so the mistake shows at load and not at connect:
- IAM: `outbox.publisher.root_ca_bundle` with `allow_insecure_broker` and a `nats://` URL.
- Gateway: `tool_policy.nats.ca_file` with a `nats://` URL. This rule is stricter than necessary: `nats://` with TLS after INFO still works against a broker that offers TLS. No chart or ops config uses this combination.

Discovery change to know: with TLS after INFO, 0.53 takes discovered servers only from the INFO inside TLS, and it verifies them by name. This can reduce failover with a single configured URL on nats-server before 2.12.

## Verification

In `rs/`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo deny check`, `cargo machete` and `cargo metadata --locked` pass. `cargo nextest run --workspace` passed 3247 tests. Docker-gated tests that were flaky passed on retry. `cargo tree -i aws-lc-rs`, `-i openssl-sys` and `-i native-tls` are empty.

An adversarial review checked the reqwest 0.13.5 trust path, every client build site, the runtime image CA store, and the jsonwebtoken diff.

I found a real break on main and opened a fix. It came from the uv 0.13.9 update in PR 499.

**What broke.** uv 0.13 no longer adds the root `dev` dependency group when a workspace member runs with `--isolated`. Because of that, `paigasus-kernel-py:test` cannot find `pytest`, and it fails on every change that runs it. PR 499 and the PRs after it passed only because this task came from the cache. PR 502 was the first PR that ran the task for real. I reproduced the failure locally.

**The fix: PR 507.**
- The kernel test now runs with `--group dev`.
- The gate's pinned wrapper hash and the test case for that command are updated.
- With the flag, 151 tests pass on uv 0.13.9.

PR 507 must merge first. Then I update PRs 500, 502, 505 and 506 from main, and merge them one at a time.

content.text:
The install worked, and your git hooks still work. The `sync hooks: ❌` line does not stop anything. I read `.git/hooks` and made no changes there.

**Why lefthook gave the error:**
- The active hooks (`pre-push`, `commit-msg`) are Entire CLI wrappers. Each wrapper runs Entire and then runs the lefthook hook in `<hook>.pre-entire`. I read `pre-push.pre-entire`, and it is the lefthook script.
- `lefthook install` sees a hook that it did not write. It tries to rename that hook to `pre-push.old`, but that file already exists since 7 November. That old file is an earlier Entire wrapper with no chain step. Lefthook then stops and shows the error.

**Do not delete `pre-push.old` to clear the message.** If you delete it, lefthook moves the Entire wrapper away and installs its own `pre-push`. Entire then stops pushing session logs. Lefthook's commit-msg and pre-push checks run in both cases. So the message is noise in this setup, and you can leave it.

**The package changes are correct.** Your `ts/node_modules` came from before the sweep. pnpm installed what the unchanged lockfile on main specifies, for example `@types/node` 26.6.6 and `semantic-release` 26.0.1.
